Thanks for the initial RFP attachments. Before we move the SOW review to procurement, two quick clarifications on the SLA section so we can map to our internal monitoring:

- Measurement window: do you measure uptime/latency per calendar day, rolling 30-day window, or monthly calendar period?

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High level answers attached and below; we also attached an editable spreadsheet mapping our metrics to your RFP fields (RFP_Response_SLA_Table.xlsx).

Summary:
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window is our default for credit calculations; we provide calendar-month summaries for reporting.
- Latency percentile: production p99 is our primary latency SLO for user-facing endpoints; p95 is reported for operational dashboards.
- Sampling: primary measurement is production telemetry with a minimum sampling policy (default 1% of production requests per region) plus continuous synthetic probes to validate edge cases.
- Service credits: credits are computed based on region-level availability shortfall measured over the rolling 30-day window; example calculation included in the spreadsheet.

Samantha — expanding on Ben's summary with concrete measurement details you can include in the RFP packet. Attached: SLA_Measurement_Methodology_v2.pdf.

Key items to include in your evaluation:
1) Measurement sources
   - Production telemetry (preferred): we instrument request traces at the edge and aggregate latency histograms per-route, per-region. Our default sampling rate for persistent measurement is 1% of successful requests per region; for high-traffic routes we auto-scale sampling to maintain stable histograms.
   - Synthetic probes: continuous health probes run from multiple regions to catch routing/edge failures not seen in sampled production telemetry. Probes are used for detection and alerting, not as the primary basis for credit calculations unless production telemetry is unavailable.

2) Time alignment and aggregation
   - Timestamps normalized to UTC; measurements are bucketed into 1-minute rollups, then aggregated into 5-minute windows for outlier smoothing.
   - Service credit evaluation uses a rolling 30-day window with per-region aggregation. We report both rolling-30 and calendar-month views for transparency.

3) Latency percentiles and outliers
   - SLO: p99 latency per-route for user-facing text generation endpoints. We compute percentiles using HDR histograms on the aggregated 1-minute buckets.
   - Outliers caused by transient upstream dependency failures are excluded if traced to third-party errors (we keep an exclusion log).

4) Credit calculation (example)
   - If availability (measured as successful request rate) for region eu-west-1 over the rolling 30-day window drops below 99.95%, credit = (99.95 - measured_availability) / 99.95 * monthly_fee * credit_multiplier (region weighting applied). Cap is 50% of monthly fee per SLA terms. Spreadsheet includes numeric example.

5) Maintenance and scheduled downtime
   - Weekly maintenance windows (default 30 mins/region/week) are excluded from measurement; extended maintenance is pre-notified and carved out per MSA.

6) Auditability and logs
   - We retain SLA telemetry and raw trace aggregates for 13 months by default; we can provide aggregated CSV extracts and signed attestations for audit.

If you need, we can provide a small sample CSV showing the 1-minute rollups and the derived p99 calculation.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom / Samantha — quick legal points to include in your questionnaire mapping: 

1) Credit cap: our standard position is a 50% cap of the monthly recurring fee per region for SLA-related service credits. We are willing to discuss an increased cap for enterprise customers under bespoke commercial terms.
2) Notice & verification: claim must be submitted in writing within 30 days of the incident window and include the signed telemetry extract described by procurement. We will validate within 15 business days and calculate credits per the published methodology.
3) Exclusions: force majeure, customer-caused misconfiguration, or scheduled maintenance with prior notice are excluded.

We can add the exact credit calculation clause to the PSA/MSA if you move to a term sheet. We will also provide a link to our SOC2 Type II report and instructions for a limited audit request under NDA.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
